key_insight: DiSH stabilizes LLM-based solver refinement by controlling both the direction and scope of edits, reducing feasibility oscillation while improving optimization performance.
engineering_relevance: For combinatorial optimization pipelines, DiSH offers a more reliable and token-efficient way to iteratively refine heuristics without repeatedly breaking previously validated behavior.
method: Selects representative failure cases instead of using full feedback
Progressively narrows the revision scope as feasible solver behavior accumulates
Uses a harness to jointly control update direction and edit breadth
evidence_signal: Across nine combinatorial optimization benchmarks, DiSH improved QYI scores, reduced feasibility oscillation, and cut feedback token use by about half versus prior full-feedback methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on good failure selection and scope control, so overly narrow revisions could miss important edge cases or slow recovery from deeper solver issues.
paper_title: Harnessing LLMs with Direction-Scope Control for Combinatorial Solver Refinement
